To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clomipraminetreated rats show significant decrease in the levels of serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine in discrete brain regions.
the levels of monoamines are decreased in discrete brain regions of clomipramined induced animal model of endogenous depression.
the dysfunction of serotonin and nor-adrenaline neurotransmission is involved, while dopamine neurotransmission is less involved in the clomiparame-induced animal model of endogenous depression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurochemical changes in a novel rat animal model of depression.
the neurochemical basis of the animal model of depression.
elucidating the pathogenesis of human depression and developing a suitable animal model of endogenous depression for the evaluation of novel antidepressants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dysfunction of serotenergic and noradrenerigic neurotransmission is involved with lesser involvement of dopamine neurotransmission in the pathogenesis and etiology of endogenous depression.
the clomipranine induced animal model of depression is a useful model to study the pathogenesis of endogenous depression.
the dysfunction in the levels of serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine are involved in the pathophysiology of depression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

clomipramin-induced animal model of depression may be a useful model to test the efficacy of antidepressants and to investigate the mechanism of action of antidepressants in the treatment of depression.
the dysfunction in serotonin and noradrenline transmission may be responsible for the behavioral abnormalities seen in this model of endogenous depression.

the dysfunction of serotonin and nor-epinephrine neurotransmission may play a major role in the pathophysiology of depression and the dysfunction of dopaminergic system may be secondary to the dysfunction of serotonic and nor-epi-nephrine system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clomipramines can be used as a model for studying the neurochemical basis of human depression.
the dysfunction of monoaminergic neurotransmission can lead to depression and the treatment with antidepressants can reverse the dysfunction.
this model of depression is a good model of endogenous depression.
